A special interest in laparoscopy can indeed impact the treatment of acute cholecystitis. While laparoscopic cholecystectomy is often considered the gold standard for treating acute cholecystitis, patients with acute cholecystitis who have a strong interest in laparoscopy may be more likely to undergo successful laparoscopic treatment.

This is because surgeons with an interest in laparoscopy are likely to be skilled and experienced in performing laparoscopic procedures. Additionally, these surgeons may take the time to fully understand and address any specific concerns or needs of their patients, which can lead to improved outcomes.

However, it's essential to note that the length of hospital stay is influenced more by patient factors in a multivariate model, rather than just the interest in laparoscopy. This means that even if a patient has a strong interest in laparoscopy and undergoes successful laparoscopic cholecystectomy, their overall outcome may not be improved.

In summary, having a special interest in laparoscopy can be beneficial for patients with acute cholecystitis who are undergoing treatment, but it is not the sole determining factor. A thorough evaluation of patient needs and circumstances is also crucial to ensure optimal outcomes.
